Alex: Quick sync — I ran a streaming vs non-streaming sweep for llama-2-13b quant variants (int8/int4) across A100 (us-west1), RTX6000 (eu-west2), and T4 (us-east1). Uploading the distilled charts to the perf dash: https://dash.redwood/perf/llama2-13b/2200001234. TL;DR: streaming lowers p50 by ~20–30ms vs non-stream but drops peak throughput by ~15–25% depending on kernel and device. T4 shows a small quality regression with aggressive int4.

Marta: nice, can you paste the perf table here so the team can eyeball numbers? :eyes:

Alex: sure — small paste from the run (tokens/sec = token emission across concurrent clients):
```
A100 (us-west1)  | streaming: p50=110ms  p95=380ms  throughput=4200 tok/s
A100 (us-west1)  | non-stream: p50=135ms  p95=410ms  throughput=5200 tok/s
RTX6000 (eu-west2)| streaming: p50=130ms  p95=420ms  throughput=3600 tok/s
RTX6000 (eu-west2)| non-stream: p50=165ms  p95=460ms  throughput=4400 tok/s
T4 (us-east1)     | streaming: p50=210ms  p95=740ms  throughput=1500 tok/s
T4 (us-east1)     | non-stream: p50=260ms  p95=820ms  throughput=1900 tok/s
```

Devon: interesting — so streaming consistently lowers median latency but sacrifices peak throughput. Any kernel differences between devices or configs that explain the delta?

Alex: yes — on A100 and RTX6000 we hit the cuBLAS-optimized attention kernels (and fused rotary ops) which keep single-token latency low; streaming lets us amortize KV cache use and small-step decoding. On T4 the runtime fell back to baseline CUDA kernels and the overhead per micro-batch is higher, so streaming's per-token overhead doesn't pay off as well. Also non-stream dispatch batches more tokens per call which gives higher GPU utilization for lower-end cards.

Len: did you try different quant levels? any quality regressions worth flagging?

Alex: ran quick evals on our standard summarization prompt-set (n=500). Short summary: int8 (GPTQ-like) vs int4 (aggressive LUT) — results below (ROUGE-L approximate):
```
A100 int8  -> ROUGE-L=27.9
A100 int4  -> ROUGE-L=27.5  (delta -0.4)
RTX6000 int8 -> ROUGE-L=27.6
RTX6000 int4 -> ROUGE-L=27.1  (delta -0.5)
T4 int8 -> ROUGE-L=27.2
T4 int4 -> ROUGE-L=26.3  (delta -0.9)  <-- noticeable drop
```
So quality looks stable on A100/RTX6000 for int4 within our tolerance; T4 int4 is marginal. Perplexity trends match — bigger bump on T4 int4.

Marta: thanks. any quick runtime knobs to improve T4 streaming perf without increasing quality loss?

Alex: a few pragmatic knobs: increase streaming chunk size from 8->16 tokens to amortize kernel launch overhead; prefer fp16 (int8) path for T4 when quality matters; reduce max concurrent streams per GPU (so each stream gets more batch accumulation); and, if feasible, pin to a model variant with KV-cache optimizations (seq_len=512). Example config we tested:
```json
{"stream_chunk_tokens":16, "max_concurrent_streams":8, "prefer_quant": "int8", "seq_len":512}
```
This moved T4 streaming p50 ~ -30ms and throughput up ~10% in our microbench.

CI-bot: Perf sweep PR #432 completed — artifacts: https://ci.redwood/perf/432/ (includes raw traces + flamegraphs) :white_check_mark:

Devon: can we add these findings to the model-onboarding checklist? would be great to have recommended defaults per GPU (stream vs non-stream).

Alex: absolutely — I'll add a short blurb to the onboarding doc and file an issue to centralize kernel + quant recommendations. Filing INF ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1234 :spiral_note_pad: 

Marta: sweet, thanks Alex. can you also attach the p50/p95 PNGs to the ticket? :thumbsup:

Alex: yup — uploading now. Will post results in the onboarding doc PR when done.
